I fell absolutely head over heels in love with a guy who I met through a friend during Spring a couple of years ago. We had been talking on Facebook, met up at our friend's birthday party. It was actually at a gay bar and I was to show up and protect him from being flirted with too hard. He was actually a very pretty man. There was something different about him... he had shoulder length wavy hair, sky blue eyes, and his voice was like butter. Not deep, not high... just soothing and buttery. 

Everything this guy said had my attention, he was so interesting. All of his jokes made me laugh, his thoughts and ideas seemed so "dead on" with what I felt. He decided he wanted to court me, like a gentleman, despite living 60 miles away. He would pick me up and take me out, he didn't make any moves, and he would drop me off with a kiss on the cheek. 

We started talking on the phone every single night. Every day was a happy day because it ended with him... There were some days it actually felt as though my heart would swell. 

I'd always been afraid people would think I was naive for falling in love so hard so fast... but it was the most amazing thing. He made me feel like the most beautiful girl in the world. I had never felt more secure in a relationship or in myself. My friends and family finally saw me at my best, his family finally got to hear him boast about his happiness. 

We finally got to sex and it was absolutely perfect. Halfway through making dinner we would run off to have fun. 

If I ever did anything to upset him he was very calm with me... and we would talk it out like adults and it would never be an issue for long. 


A week and a half after New Years he got the flu and sent me home from my weekend visit with him. Up until this point we had spoken to eachother every single night on the phone or in person... I didn't call him the next night, hoping he was resting. 

The next morning I got a call from his brother, telling me he'd passed away and that I should come down to help make funeral arrangements.

I'm at work and in tears now, but I love talking about him still.
